samples.summary: Cycle guard added to every view-side blockParentMap walk, but `Doc.findBlockInCells` still recurses over the same map unbounded — a cyclic chain overflows the stack instead of returning undefined
samples.evidence: This delta extends the `resolveNestedTableLayout` cycle guard to two more walks (`peer-cursor.ts:129`, `selection.ts:133`), on the stated premise that a looping parent chain is representable because block ids come verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes. The model-side walk over the *same* data never got that guard: `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:276` does `tableBlock = this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId);` with no visited set, so for a map containing a->b and b->a the call recurses forever and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the recursive-walk fallback at :287 can run. The map it reads is exactly the layout-derived, peer-id-keyed map: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1703` pushes the merged body+header+footer `blockParentMap` into `doc.setBlockParentMap`, and the merge across regions makes an A->B / B->A pair even easier to form than within one region. `findBlockInCells` is on the hot path for every `doc.getBlock`/`findBlock` of a cell block (typing, deletion, paste), so the crash is reachable wherever the delta's own threat model says the cycle is. Fix belongs on document.ts, mirroring the `seen` set the other three walks now carry (see `range-slices.ts:80` which already does).

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `Doc.findBlockInCells` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:261-290) reads `this._blockParentMap` at :265 and recurses at :276 via `tableBlock = this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId);` with no visited set and no depth bound; a cyclic pair (a->b, b->a) re-enters forever and never reaches the parent-map-independent fallback at :287-289, so it throws RangeError instead of returning undefined. Every sibling walk over the same map carries a `seen` guard — table-layout.ts:488-495 (whose comment at :480-486 states block ids arrive verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes so a looping parent chain is representable), range-slices.ts:80-92, selection.ts:132-137, peer-cursor.ts:128-135, text-editor.ts:3894-3924 — confirming the codebase's own threat model treats the cycle as reachable. The map is the same one: editor.ts:1696-1703 merges body+header+footer maps and calls doc.setBlockParentMap, and layout.ts:514-517 merges per-table maps keyed by raw block id with no de-duplication or cycle rejection, so a cross-region duplicated id yields an A->B/B->A pair. The site is on the ordinary lookup path: getBlock (:236) and findBlock (:254) both fall through to findBlockInCells for any cell block. No upstream guard makes it unreachable, so no refutation ground applies; the fix belongs on document.ts mirroring the `seen` set the other walks carry.

mergedFrom.summary: The cell-internal branch of `getSelectedText()` uses the same flat `layout.blocks.find()` on `startCellInfo.tableBlockId`, so plain-text copy of an ordinary text selection inside a nested table cell is empty

finding.summary: `Selection.getSelectedText()` still resolves a cell rectangle with the flat `layout.blocks.find()` this change replaced everywhere else — a nested-table rectangle yields empty `text/plain` on copy AND on cut
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:761-763: `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId); if (!lb?.block.tableData) return '';`. A nested table block is not a member of `layout.blocks` (that is the whole premise of the diff's fixes to `normalizeRange` at selection.ts:128 and `getSelectedTableCells` at text-editor.ts:4331), so this returns `''`. Both clipboard writers call it unconditionally right after the now-fixed rich flavour: text-editor.ts:1439 (copy) and text-editor.ts:1482 (cut). Cut then calls `this.deleteSelection()` at text-editor.ts:1484, so a user cutting a cell rectangle inside a nested table — a gesture this change newly makes reachable by shift+click — loses the content for any external paste target that only reads `text/plain`. Fix belongs here: use `resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` as the fallback, exactly as the two sibling sites now do.

verdict.reason: The claimed evidence is not in the repository. selection.ts:760-765 is `getNormalizedRange()` (a delegate to `normalizeRange`), not the quoted `layout.blocks.find(...)` / `if (!lb?.block.tableData) return ''` snippet. The actual `getSelectedText()` begins at selection.ts:777 and its cell-range branch at selection.ts:788-791 already reads `layout.blocks.find(...)?.block.tableData ?? resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` — precisely the fix the finding prescribes — with a comment at selection.ts:784-787 citing the same #1049 bug. The cell-internal branch is nested-aware too (selection.ts:816-821), matching the sibling sites at selection.ts:157 and text-editor.ts:4333. Because `getSelectedText()` resolves nested tables, the downstream consequence (empty `text/plain` at the copy writer text-editor.ts:1439 and the cut writer text-editor.ts:1482, followed by deleteSelection) does not occur. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: The cycle guard the diff adds to three parent-chain walks is bypassed by two unguarded walks in the very function it edited (`normalizeRange`), which hang on the same cyclic `blockParentMap`
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:147-157: `while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex((lb) => lb.block.id === anchorTopId) === -1) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(anchorTopId); if (!parentInfo) break; anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` (and the identical focus walk at :153). With the cyclic map the diff's own new test constructs (`a -> b -> a`, nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:253-258) neither id is ever found in `layout.blocks`, `parentInfo` is always defined, and the loop never terminates. This runs on every non-cell-range selection normalization — i.e. on virtually every render with a selection — so it is strictly more reachable than the `resolveNestedTableLayout` walk the diff hardened. Fix belongs on these two loops (add the same `seen` set).

verdict.reason: The two "unguarded" parent-chain loops the finding quotes do not exist in the working tree. selection.ts:146-163 is the tableCellRange early-return branch (flat lookup + resolveNestedTableLayout fallback + normalizeCellRange) and contains no while loop; normalizeRange contains no while loop anywhere. The anchor and focus walks are factored into the guarded helper walkToTopLevelBlockId (selection.ts:127-140), which holds the same cycle guard the finding demands: `const seen = new Set<string>([id])` (:132), `if (!parentInfo || seen.has(parentInfo.tableBlockId)) break;` (:135), `seen.add(id)` (:138). Both call sites go through it — anchor at :173-176, focus at :177-180 — and anchorTopId/focusTopId are const results of that helper, not mutated loop variables. A repo-wide grep for anchorTopId/focusTopId returns only these plus range-slices.ts:194-197, which walks via its own seen-guarded topLevelBlockId (range-slices.ts:80-92). The cyclic map cited (x -> a -> b -> a) is in fact asserted against this very path: nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:288-310 expects selection.getNormalizedRange(cyclicLayout()) to return null. The sibling walks are likewise guarded (table-layout.ts:487-495, peer-cursor.ts:128-136). The quoted evidence describes pre-change code the diff replaced.

finding.summary: `resolvePositionPixel()` walks the same peer-written parent chain with an unguarded `while (true)` and an unbounded `unshift`, so the hang the new guard prevents is still reachable through peer cursor painting
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:122-127: `while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(currentTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo); currentTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`. Identical shape to the walk hardened at table-layout.ts:489 and to `findOuterCellAddress`/`findOutermostTableId` in text-editor.ts; on a cyclic chain it spins forever and additionally grows `nestingPath` without bound (OOM as well as hang). This path runs per render for the local caret and for every peer cursor/selection, i.e. it is driven by remote presence data. Fix belongs on this loop.

verdict.reason: The finding alleges an unguarded `while (true)` parent-chain walk in `resolvePositionPixel()`, quoting a loop body with no cycle check. The code is not as described. The actual loop at packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:129-136 contains the cycle guard: `seenTableIds` is seeded at line 128 (`new Set<string>([currentTableId])`), the walk bails with `return undefined` at line 132 (`if (seenTableIds.has(parentInfo.tableBlockId)) return undefined;`) BEFORE the `nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo)` on line 133, and each visited id is recorded at line 135. The reviewer's quoted evidence omits exactly lines 128, 132 and 135 — the guard it claims is absent. Termination is sound: each non-returning iteration adds a distinct id to `seenTableIds`, so the walk is bounded by `blockParentMap.size` and `nestingPath` is likewise bounded, making both the alleged hang and the alleged unbounded-growth OOM unreachable. This is the same hardening as the sites the finding cites as the contrast: table-layout.ts:489-495 (`resolveNestedTableLayout`) uses the identical `seen`/`return undefined` shape, and text-editor.ts:3895-3904 and 3920-3925 guard `findOuterCellAddress`/`findOutermostTableId` the same way; the comment at peer-cursor.ts:122-127 explicitly names `resolveNestedTableLayout` as the pattern it mirrors. I also confirmed there is no second, unguarded copy of the function: `resolvePositionPixel` is defined once (peer-cursor.ts:104), the only other hit being an archived task document (docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260324-docs-remote-cursor-todo.md:192), which is prose rather than executed code.
